Section.name: High-Level Description
Section.IntroParagraph: RagBrain is a personal RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) pipeline designed for learning and daily use. It ingests three primary data sources—ChatGPT conversation history, YouTube transcripts from followed creators, and personal markdown notes— normalizes them into searchable chunks, and exposes every stage of the pipeline for inspection and tuning. The core innovation is a summarization-first approach: verbose conversations are condensed into compact, deduplicated knowledge chunks while maintaining citations back to original sources. The system prioritizes transparency (see why something was retrieved), experimentation (swap LLMs at any stage), and practical daily use via MCP integration with Cursor/Cline.

SupportingBullets.Bullet: Primary user: Solo developer learning RAG concepts by building
Core journey: Ask a question → get relevant context with source citations → understand retrieval logic
Business value: Eliminate repeated conversations, surface relevant past knowledge, create personal "second brain"
Out of scope (V1): Real-time web scraping, multi-user support, production deployment
Constraints: TypeScript-first architecture, local-first (runs on desktop with Ollama), learning over polish

Goals.Goal: Ingest and normalize ChatGPT export JSON into summarized, deduplicated chunks with source citations
Ingest YouTube transcripts with chapter-aware chunking and interest-based ranking
Provide full pipeline transparency: visualize how data was ingested, chunked, embedded, and retrieved
Enable LLM experimentation: easily swap models (local Ollama vs OpenRouter) at each pipeline stage
Expose MCP endpoint for querying from Cursor/Cline with relevant context injection
Create a "homepage/news" view showing recent ingested content organized by topics/tags
Maintain ground truth: all summarized content links back to original source material
Learn by doing: understand every component, avoid magic black-box libraries

NonGoals.NonGoal: Production-grade scalability (this is a personal tool)
Real-time ingestion (batch processing is fine for V1)
Mobile app or native desktop app
Automatic YouTube subscription syncing (manual URL input for V1)
Using single "magic" libraries that hide the pipeline (e.g., LangChain abstractions)

Phase.name: ChatGPT History Ingestion
Phase.Description: Core pipeline for ingesting, summarizing, and deduplicating ChatGPT conversation exports

Row.UserStory: As a user, I want to upload my ChatGPT JSON export so that my past conversations become searchable.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Given a valid conversations.json file, when I upload it via UI or CLI, then it is parsed and queued for processing.
The system extracts: conversation title, creation date, all message pairs (user + assistant).
Invalid JSON files show clear error messages.

Row.UserStory: As a user, I want each conversation summarized into compact chunks so that verbose/repetitive content is condensed.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Given a conversation with multiple message pairs, when processed, then the system generates 1-N summary chunks.
Each summary chunk contains: summary text, topic tags, source conversation ID, message range covered.
Long conversations (>20 messages) are split into logical topic-based chunks.
Summary preserves key decisions, code snippets, and actionable items.

Knobs.Knob: LLM used for summarization (local vs API)

Row.UserStory: As a user, I want similar summary chunks grouped at retrieval time so that I don't see redundant near-duplicate results.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Given search results with similar chunks, when displayed, then they are grouped together.
Grouped results show all source citations from contributing chunks.
User can expand group to see individual chunks if needed.
Similarity threshold for grouping is configurable.

EdgeCases.EdgeCase: Three+ chunks all similar to each other
Chunks similar in topic but contradictory in content

Row.Note: KISS Decision: Ingestion-time dedup (synthesizing similar chunks into master chunks) moved to Future Roadmap. V1 uses retrieval-time grouping only.

Knobs.Knob: Cosine similarity threshold for grouping results (0.0-1.0)

FutureRequirement.UserStory: As a user, I want similar chunks merged during ingestion so the database is cleaner.
FutureRequirement.Description: Synthesize chunks with 80%+ overlap into a single "master chunk" that preserves unique content from each source. More complex but results in cleaner index.

Row.UserStory: As a user, I want to see the original conversation when viewing a summary so that I can verify or dive deeper.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Given a summary chunk displayed in UI, when I click "View Source", then the original conversation messages are shown.
For merged chunks, all source conversations are accessible.
Original content is stored separately from summaries (not discarded).

EdgeCases.EdgeCase: Source conversation was in a previous export (incremental ingestion)

Row.UserStory: As a user, I want chunks embedded and indexed so that semantic search works.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Given processed chunks, when embedding runs, then vectors are stored in LanceDB.
Metadata stored with vectors: source_type, tags, created_at, source_ids, chunk_type.
Embedding model is configurable (local sentence-transformers or API).

Phase.name: YouTube Transcript Ingestion
Phase.Description: Ingest YouTube transcripts with chapter-aware chunking and interest ranking

Row.UserStory: As a user, I want to input a YouTube URL and have the transcript fetched and parsed.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Given a valid YouTube URL, when I submit it, then transcript is fetched (via yt-dlp or API).
Chapter markers are extracted if available.
Video metadata stored: title, channel, duration, upload date, URL.

Row.UserStory: As a user, I want transcripts chunked hierarchically by chapters so that I can find specific topics while retaining broader context.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Given a video with chapters, when processed, then each chapter becomes a "parent" chunk with summary.
Long chapters (>2 min transcript) generate "child" sub-chunks with semantic overlap.
Child chunks reference their parent chapter for context retrieval.
Videos without chapters are chunked by semantic boundaries (~500 tokens, 100 overlap).
Each chunk includes: chapter title, timestamp range, video source reference, parent_id (if child).
UI shows parent/child relationship visually (expandable tree or nested cards).

Knobs.Knob: Chapter length (seconds) before creating child sub-chunks
When retrieving child, also return parent context (boolean)

Row.UIVisualization: Hierarchical view showing Chapter (Parent) → Sub-chunks (Children) relationship. Clicking a child chunk shows both its content AND the parent chapter summary.

Row.UserStory: As a user, I want chunks summarized and tagged so that I can quickly scan what a video covers.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Given video chunks, when summarized, then each has a 1-2 sentence summary.
Topic tags are extracted and normalized.
Summaries are searchable alongside ChatGPT content.

Row.UserStory: As a user, I want to rank content by my interests so that relevant topics surface first.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Given my interest profile (positive/negative keywords), when viewing digests, then content is sorted by relevance.
Interest profile is editable via UI.
Negative keywords push content down in ranking.

EdgeCases.EdgeCase: No interest profile defined (show all equally)
Content matches both positive and negative keywords

Knobs.Knob: How much interest affects ranking vs recency

Phase.name: Markdown Notes Ingestion
Phase.Description: Ingest personal markdown notes, bugs, tickets from various folders

Row.UserStory: As a user, I want to select folders of markdown files to ingest into the knowledge base.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Given a folder path, when I add it via UI, then all .md files are parsed.
Frontmatter (YAML) is extracted as metadata if present.
File path and name are preserved as metadata.
After ingestion, parsed data is normalized (doesn't need original folder).

Row.UserStory: As a user, I want my notes chunked intelligently so that code blocks and context are preserved.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Markdown headers (##, ###) create natural chunk boundaries.
Code blocks are kept intact within chunks when possible.
Very long sections are split with overlap.

Row.UserStory: As a user, I want notes about bugs/quirks surfaced when I encounter similar issues.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Notes tagged with "bug", "quirk", "workaround" are specially indexed.
Error messages or stack traces in notes are extractable.
Query "I'm seeing error X" matches relevant past bug notes.

Phase.name: Query and Retrieval
Phase.Description: Search, retrieve, and understand why results were returned

Row.UserStory: As a user, I want to ask natural language questions and get relevant chunks back.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Given a query, when I search, then top-k relevant chunks are returned.
Results show: summary, source type, relevance score, tags.
Hybrid search: semantic similarity + tag/metadata filtering.

Row.UserStory: As a user, I want to see WHY a chunk was retrieved so I can understand and tune the system.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Given search results, when I expand a result, then I see: similarity score, matching terms, pipeline trace.
Pipeline trace shows: how chunk was created, which model summarized it, dedup history.
I can see the embedding vector (or a visualization of it).

Row.UserStory: As a user, I want retrieved chunks reranked for quality before being used in generation.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Given initial retrieval results, when reranking is enabled, then a reranker model rescores them.
Reranking is optional and togglable.
Before/after reranking scores are visible.

Row.UserStory: As a user, I want smart deduplication at retrieval time so similar results are merged.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Given multiple similar results, when retrieval dedup is on, then they are grouped/merged.
Merged results show all sources that contributed.
This is in addition to ingestion-time dedup.

Phase.name: Interface and Integration
Phase.Description: Web UI, CLI, and MCP integration

Row.UserStory: As a user, I want a web UI to manage ingestion, search, and view the pipeline.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Next.js app with pages for: Ingest, Search, Pipeline View, Settings.
Catppuccin theme inherited from flashbuild-llmcomparer base.
Responsive design for desktop use.

Row.UserStory: As a user, I want a "homepage/news" view showing recent ingested content organized by topics.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Homepage shows recently ingested content grouped by source type.
Content is sortable by: date, relevance to interests, source.
Tags are clickable to filter.
YouTube chapters show as expandable cards with timestamps.

Row.UserStory: As a user, I want to query via MCP from Cursor/Cline so context is injected into my coding sessions.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: MCP server exposes a "search" tool that takes a query and returns relevant chunks.
Chunks are formatted for LLM context injection.
Source citations are included in response.

Row.UserStory: As a user, I want a chat interface to ask questions and get answers with RAG context.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Chat UI in web app allows conversational queries.
Retrieved context is shown alongside generated answer.
Model used for generation is selectable (Ollama local or OpenRouter).

Row.UserStory: As a user, I want CLI commands for all operations so I can script and automate.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: CLI supports: ingest, search, config, status commands.
Output is JSON-friendly for scripting.
Daemon mode available for background processing.

Row.UserStory: As a user, I want to visualize the entire pipeline so I understand data flow.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Pipeline diagram shows: Ingest → Normalize → Summarize → Dedupe → Chunk → Embed → Index.
Each stage shows item counts and status.
Clicking a stage shows detailed logs/stats.

Row.UserStory: As a user, I want to trace any chunk back through the pipeline to see its history via a waterfall view.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Given any indexed chunk, when I click it, then I see a "Waterfall Trace" of its journey.
Waterfall shows: [Load File] → [Split into N Chunks] → [Summarize] → [Embed via Model X] → [Saved to DB].
Each step is expandable to show details (e.g., summarization prompt/response).
I can see the raw embedding vector values for the chunk.
Source citation is immediately visible (link to original conversation/video/note).
For hierarchical chunks: parent/child relationship shown in trace.

Row.UISpecification: Clicking any chunk in search results or browse view opens a detail panel with: 1. Chunk content (summary) 2. Source citation (clickable link to original) 3. Waterfall trace (collapsible steps) 4. Raw vector values (collapsible, for learning/debugging) 5. Metadata (tags, created_at, embedding model, etc.)

Row.UserStory: As a user, I want to compare LLM performance at each pipeline stage.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: For summarization: compare outputs from different models side-by-side.
Track: tokens used, latency, output quality (manual rating).
Reuse LLM comparison infrastructure from flashbuild-llmcomparer.

Row.UserStory: As a user, I want all configuration in .env files that I can inspect and modify.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: .env.local contains all knobs with clear comments.
UI settings panel syncs with .env values.
Changes require explicit restart/reload for safety.

UserFlow.Name: First-Time ChatGPT Ingestion
UserFlow.Goal: User imports their ChatGPT history and sees summarized, searchable knowledge

Steps.Step: User exports conversations.json from ChatGPT settings
User uploads file via UI or provides path via CLI
System parses JSON, shows conversation count and preview
User confirms ingestion, selects LLM for summarization
Pipeline processes: normalize → summarize → dedupe → embed
Progress shown in real-time with stage completion
User sees summary: X conversations → Y unique chunks, Z duplicates merged
User tests with a search query, sees results with sources

DecisionPoints.DecisionPoint: Step 4: User can adjust summarization model and parameters
Step 7: User can drill into any chunk to see its pipeline trace

ExitStates.ExitState: Knowledge base populated, ready for queries
Ingestion failed with actionable error message

UserFlow.Name: Query via MCP in Cursor
UserFlow.Goal: User asks a question in Cursor and gets relevant context from their knowledge base

EntryPoints.EntryPoint: Cursor chat with MCP tool available

Steps.Step: User types question referencing past work (e.g., "How did I handle auth in that project?")
Cursor invokes RagBrain MCP search tool
RagBrain retrieves relevant chunks, reranks, dedupes
Chunks returned with source citations
Cursor LLM uses context to generate helpful response
User sees answer with clickable source links

ExitStates.ExitState: Relevant context injected, useful answer generated
No matching content, user prompted to refine query

UserFlow.Name: Daily Digest / Homepage View
UserFlow.Goal: User sees what's new and relevant from recently ingested content

Steps.Step: User opens RagBrain homepage
System shows recent ingestions grouped by source (YouTube, ChatGPT, Notes)
YouTube content shows as chapter cards with thumbnails
User filters by interest tags or sorts by relevance
User clicks a chapter to see summary and option to watch at timestamp
User marks items as "reviewed" or "save for later"

ExitStates.ExitState: User caught up on relevant new content

UserFlow.Name: Pipeline Debugging
UserFlow.Goal: User understands why a specific result was (or wasn't) retrieved

Steps.Step: User performs a search, notices unexpected result
User clicks "Inspect" on the result
System shows: similarity score, matching terms, chunk metadata
User clicks "View Pipeline Trace"
System shows: original source → summarization output → merge history → embedding
User identifies issue (e.g., poor summary, wrong tags)
User adjusts relevant knob (e.g., summarization prompt)
User re-processes affected content with new settings

ExitStates.ExitState: User understands retrieval logic, improves system

Section.name: Architecture and Tech Options
Section.ArchitectureOverview: TypeScript-first monorepo with Next.js frontend, Node.js backend services, and Python wrappers only for heavy NLP tasks. Local-first design running on desktop alongside Ollama. Embedded LanceDB for vector storage.

Component.Name: Frontend
Component.Rationale: Already have flashbuild-llmcomparer as base, familiar stack, good DX

Component.Name: Vector Database
Component.Rationale: Embedded (no server), first-class TypeScript SDK, inspectable data files, supports metadata filtering. Perfect for "see all the knobs" philosophy.
Component.WhyThisAligns: LanceDB stores data as Parquet files you can literally browse in a folder. This aligns with the "learning by seeing" goal — you can open the files, inspect vectors, understand the format. ChromaDB runs as a service which hides the data. For a "first year CS student" approach, seeing the files is more educational than interacting with an opaque database service.

Alternatives.Alternative: Python-first, runs as service, less transparent
Too much ops overhead for learning project

Component.Name: Metadata Storage
Component.Rationale: Simple, embedded, TypeScript-friendly. Stores: source documents, pipeline traces, chunk metadata, user settings.

Component.Name: LLM Integration
Component.Rationale: Ollama already running on desktop. OpenRouter for free-tier models and comparison. Reuse OpenRouter integration from flashbuild-llmcomparer.

Component.Name: Embedding Models

Options.Option: sentence-transformers via Python wrapper, or Xenova/transformers.js
OpenAI embeddings via OpenRouter, or free alternatives

Component.Recommendation: Start with transformers.js for pure TS, add Python for quality comparison

Component.Name: YouTube Transcripts
Component.Rationale: Battle-tested, handles all edge cases, extracts chapters

Component.Name: MCP Server
Component.Rationale: Official SDK, TypeScript-native, easy integration with Cursor/Cline
Component.Architecture: Separate package in monorepo (apps/mcp/) that imports and calls the internal pipeline package (packages/core/). This keeps MCP concerns isolated while sharing all the retrieval logic.

SubDirectory.name: core/
SubDirectory.description: Shared pipeline logic (ingest, chunk, embed, retrieve)

Section.name: Metrics and Instrumentation
Section.MetricsPhilosophy: Focus on learning and debugging, not production monitoring. Track what helps understand and improve the pipeline.

Metric.Name: Deduplication Rate
Metric.Definition: Percentage of chunks merged during dedup (ingestion + retrieval)

Metric.Name: Retrieval Relevance
Metric.Definition: User feedback (thumbs up/down) on search results

Metric.Name: LLM Cost/Performance
Metric.Definition: Tokens used, latency, per model per stage

Metric.Name: Index Size
Metric.Definition: Total chunks, unique sources, storage used

Risk.Description: Summarization quality varies significantly between LLMs
Risk.Mitigation: Build comparison tooling early, test multiple models, allow easy switching

Risk.Description: Deduplication may merge content that should stay separate
Risk.Mitigation: Start with conservative thresholds, always preserve originals, allow manual un-merge

Risk.Description: yt-dlp may break with YouTube changes
Risk.Mitigation: Abstract behind interface, monitor for updates, have fallback transcript sources

Risk.Description: LanceDB is newer, may have edge cases
Risk.Mitigation: Keep data exports possible, could migrate to alternative if needed

Dependencies.Dependency: OpenRouter API key with free tier access
ChatGPT export (user must export from settings)

OpenQuestions.Question: Should we use a monorepo tool (Turborepo, Nx) or keep it simple with npm workspaces? Start with npm workspaces, add Turborepo if build times become an issue
How to handle incremental ChatGPT exports (new conversations only)? Hash conversation IDs, skip already-processed, allow force-reprocess
What embedding model to start with? all-MiniLM-L6-v2 via transformers.js (fast, decent quality, pure TS)
Should the MCP server run separately or be part of the Next.js app? Separate process for reliability, but shares code via packages/
